subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should the sandbox-triggered `sessions_spawn` stall be fixed with a new startup lifecycle contract, a narrower sandbox fail-fast path, or by folding it into the broader subagent lifecycle issue?
rationale: Source shows the accepted-before-sandbox-start boundary, but the remaining fix shape determines whether OpenClaw adds lifecycle event semantics or only changes sandbox startup reporting.

options.title: Adopt lifecycle contract with sandbox proof
options.body: Replace the stale lifecycle PR with a current-main implementation of typed startup/progress state and live `non-main` sandboxed subagent proof.

options.title: Keep the fix sandbox-specific
options.body: Surface Docker/sandbox startup failures through existing session status and logs without adding new lifecycle phases, accepting that broader startup silence remains separate.

options.title: Defer to broader lifecycle tracking
options.body: Keep this issue as linked evidence under https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776 and avoid a separate sandbox repair until that direction is accepted.

recommendation.title: Adopt lifecycle contract with sandbox proof
recommendation.body: Replace the stale lifecycle PR with a current-main implementation of typed startup/progress state and live `non-main` sandboxed subagent proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses subagent lifecycle and terminal outcome seams where history shows substantial ownership.
